# Career OS — Full Technical Reference for LLMs and AI Agents
## Version 2.5.0 | MIT License

> This document provides exhaustive technical context for LLMs, AI coding assistants,
> autonomous agents, and AI search systems. Updated: 2026-07.

---

## 1. Project Identity

- **Name**: Career OS
- **Tagline**: AI-powered Career Intelligence Platform
- **Version**: 2.5.0
- **Repository**: https://github.com/karthikrshet/Career-Agents
- **Primary Author**: Karthik R Shet (github.com/karthikrshet)
- **License**: MIT
- **Framework**: Next.js 14 (App Router, TypeScript)
- **Deployment Target**: Vercel (primary), any Node.js host
- **Node Requirement**: >=18.0.0

## 2. Architecture Overview

```
apps/web/                    # Next.js 14 web application
├── src/
│   ├── app/                 # App Router pages
│   │   ├── layout.tsx       # Root layout, metadata, JSON-LD, PWA
│   │   ├── page.tsx         # Dashboard (/)
│   │   ├── resume/          # Resume Studio
│   │   ├── github/          # GitHub Analyzer
│   │   ├── linkedin/        # LinkedIn Optimizer
│   │   ├── interview/       # Interview Lab
│   │   ├── tracker/         # Job Tracker (Kanban)
│   │   ├── prephub/         # Prep Hub
│   │   ├── copilot/         # Career Copilot Chat
│   │   ├── reports/         # Career Reports
│   │   ├── marketplace/     # Plugin Marketplace

│   │   ├── settings/        # Settings
│   │   ├── about/           # About & Agent Registry
│   │   ├── credits/         # Credits & OSS Stats
│   │   ├── login/           # Login (guest-first)
│   │   ├── api/             # API Routes (server-side)
│   │   │   ├── copilot/     # Streaming chat with agent router
│   │   │   ├── resume/      # Resume analysis + rewrite
│   │   │   ├── github/      # GitHub profile analysis
│   │   │   ├── linkedin/    # LinkedIn analysis
│   │   │   └── interview/   # Interview STAR evaluation
│   │   ├── robots.ts        # Auto-generates /robots.txt
│   │   └── sitemap.ts       # Auto-generates /sitemap.xml
│   ├── components/
│   │   ├── layout/          # Sidebar, Topbar, CommandPalette
│   │   ├── ui/              # Radix-based design system
│   │   └── seo/             # JSON-LD structured data
│   ├── lib/
│   │   ├── ai/              # AI router, provider manager
│   │   ├── store.ts         # Zustand global state (persisted)
│   │   ├── resume-engine.ts # Resume parsing & scoring
│   │   ├── github-api.ts    # GitHub data fetching & analysis
│   │   └── utils.ts         # Shared utilities
│   └── types/
│       └── index.ts         # All TypeScript interfaces
├── public/
│   ├── sw.js                # Production service worker
│   ├── manifest.webmanifest # PWA manifest
│   ├── llms.txt             # AI discoverability summary
│   ├── llms-full.txt        # AI discoverability full reference
│   └── icons/               # PWA icons (16, 32, 192, 512)
├── prisma/
│   └── schema.prisma        # Database schema (SQLite/PostgreSQL)
└── next.config.js           # Security headers, webpack config
```

## 3. App Router Structure

All pages use Next.js 14 App Router. Layout hierarchy:

```
layout.tsx (root — Sidebar + Toaster + JsonLd + SW registration)
└── page.tsx (Dashboard)
└── resume/page.tsx
└── github/page.tsx
└── linkedin/page.tsx
└── interview/page.tsx
└── tracker/page.tsx
└── prephub/page.tsx
└── copilot/page.tsx
└── reports/page.tsx
└── marketplace/page.tsx
└── mcp/page.tsx
└── settings/page.tsx
└── about/page.tsx
└── credits/page.tsx
└── login/page.tsx
```

Client pages use `"use client"`. Server pages (API routes, robots.ts, sitemap.ts) are pure server.

---

## 4. AI Provider System

Located in `packages/ai/` (monorepo) and `src/lib/ai/`.

### Provider Manager (`src/lib/ai/provider-manager.ts`)
- `getProvider(providerName)` returns the active provider instance
- Priority: ENV variable key → database encrypted key → user-supplied key
- Never reads localStorage on the server

### Supported Providers
| ID | Name | Default Model |
|----|------|--------------|
| `openai` | OpenAI | gpt-4o |
| `claude` | Anthropic Claude | claude-opus-4 |
| `gemini` | Google Gemini | gemini-2.5-pro |
| `groq` | Groq | llama-3.3-70b-versatile |
| `openrouter` | OpenRouter | openai/gpt-4o |
| `ollama` | Ollama (local) | llama3 |
| `lmstudio` | LM Studio (local) | local-model |
| `azure` | Azure OpenAI | gpt-4 |
| `deepseek` | DeepSeek | deepseek-chat |
| `together` | Together AI | meta-llama/Llama-3-70b |
| `mistral` | Mistral | mistral-large-latest |
| `cohere` | Cohere | command-r-plus |
| `xai` | xAI Grok | grok-beta |

Default: `claude` / `claude-opus-4`. Temperature: 0.7. Streaming: true.

### AI Flow
```
User query
    ↓
Copilot page (client) — builds context from Zustand store
    ↓
POST /api/copilot (server) — receives messages + providerConfig + context
    ↓
findBestAgents(query) — intent classifier scores 146 agents
    ↓
Load agent .md files → merge system prompts
    ↓
getProvider(providerName) → stream()
    ↓
ReadableStream SSE → client
    ↓
Streamed tokens rendered in chat UI
```

---

## 5. Agent System

### Registry
- `agent-registry.json` — 146 agent definitions (id, name, division, description, emoji, tags, skills, filename)
- `divisions.json` — 19 divisions grouping agents
- `career-os.json` — compiled master configuration (DO NOT edit manually)

### Intent Classifier (`/api/copilot/route.ts`)
Scores each agent against the user query:
- +15 if full agent name matches query
- +3 per keyword in name that appears in query (length > 3)
- +2 per tag match
- +2 per skill match
- Intent boosters: +12 for domain-specific keywords (resume→resume agents, github→github agents, etc.)
- Top 3 agents selected (score ≥ 5 threshold)
- Agent `.md` files loaded from disk, frontmatter stripped, injected as system prompt

### Agent Divisions (19 total)
Resume, GitHub, LinkedIn, Interview, Job Search, Salary, Career Planning, Company Research, Networking, Personal Branding, Skills Development, Portfolio, Open Source, Remote Work, Entrepreneurship, Academic, Bootcamp, Career Transition, Executive

---

## 6. Resume Engine

File: `src/lib/resume-engine.ts`

### Input
- Plain text extracted from PDF/DOCX/TXT/MD/RTF (via resume page upload)

### Output (`ResumeAnalysis` interface)
```typescript
{
  id: string;
  fileName: string;
  rawText: string;
  overallScore: number;      // 0-100
  atsScore: number;          // 0-100
  sections: {
    hasExperience, hasEducation, hasSkills, hasProjects, hasSummary
  };
  weakBullets: WeakBullet[]; // passive verb, no metric, vague, too short
  missingKeywords: string[];
  detectedKeywords: string[];
  recommendations: string[];
  aiRewrite?: string;
  starAnalysis?: StarAnalysisItem[];
  missingSkills?: string[];
  analyzedAt: string;
}
```

### Scoring
- ATS: keyword density, section completeness, format compliance
- Weak bullets: regex + heuristic detection of passive verbs and metrics absence
- Missing keywords: comparison against top 50 SWE job keywords

---

## 7. Interview Engine

File: `src/app/api/interview/route.ts`

Every submitted answer is evaluated by the configured AI provider.

### Evaluation Output
```json
{
  "overall": 0-100,
  "star": {
    "situation": 0-10,
    "task": 0-10,
    "action": 0-10,
    "result": 0-10
  },
  "leadership": 0-10,
  "technicalDepth": 0-10,
  "feedback": "string",
  "improvements": ["string"],
  "strengths": ["string"]
}
```

Fallback: If AI provider unavailable, returns 503 with action list (retry, switch provider, save draft). No hardcoded scores, no random values.

---

## 8. Zustand Store (`src/lib/store.ts`)

Persisted to `localStorage` under key `career-os-store`.

### Key State Slices
- `profile` — UserProfile (name, email, targetRole, targetCompany, githubUsername)
- `metrics` — CareerMetrics (careerScore, resumeScore, githubScore, linkedinScore, interviewScore)
- `resumeAnalysis` — ResumeAnalysis | null
- `GitHubAnalysis` — GitHubAnalysis | null
- `linkedinAnalysis` — LinkedInAnalysis | null
- `copilotSessions` — CopilotSession[]
- `jobApplications` — JobApplication[]
- `installedPlugins` — Record<string, boolean>
- `enabledPlugins` — Record<string, boolean>
- `interviewSessions` — InterviewSession[]
- `aiConfig` — AIProviderConfig (provider, model, temperature, streaming, apiKey)

### Actions
- `setProfile`, `updateMetrics`, `setResumeAnalysis`, `setGitHubAnalysis`, `setLinkedInAnalysis`
- `addCopilotSession`, `updateCopilotSession`, `deleteCopilotSession`, `duplicateCopilotSession`
- `addJobApplication`, `updateJobApplication`, `deleteJobApplication`
- `installPlugin`, `uninstallPlugin`, `enablePlugin`, `disablePlugin`, `updatePlugin`
- `addInterviewSession`, `updateInterviewScorecard`
- `resetProfile`

---

## 9. Plugin SDK

Plugins hook into Career Copilot system prompt via `enabledPlugins` context injection.

### Available Plugins
| ID | Name | Effect |
|----|------|--------|
| `star-coach` | STAR Behavioral Coach | Injects STAR format instructions |
| `leetcode-tracker` | LeetCode Tracker | Injects Big-O analysis instructions |
| `resume-pdf` | Resume PDF Parser | PDF layout compliance hints |
| `salary-intel` | Salary Intelligence | Compensation negotiation tactics |

Plugin lifecycle: Install → Load → Enable → Execute (inject to prompt) → Disable → Unload → Remove

---

## 10. MCP Integration

Career OS acts as an MCP server exposing 146 career agents.

### MCP Tools
- `query_agent(agentId, input)` — query specific agent
- `list_agents(division?)` — list agents by division
- `get_resume_audit(resumeText)` — run resume analysis
- `get_github_analysis(username)` — analyze GitHub profile
- `get_interview_score(question, answer)` — STAR evaluation

### Client Configurations Generated
Cursor, Claude Desktop, VS Code Continue, Windsurf, Cline, RooCode, OpenHands, Bolt, Aider

---

## 11. Database Schema (Prisma)

Supports SQLite (development) and PostgreSQL (production).

Key models: User, Session, Profile, Resume, GitHubProfile, InterviewSession, JobApplication, Plugin, AIConfig

Switch database: change `provider` in `schema.prisma` + update `DATABASE_URL`.

---

## 12. Security Model

- API keys stored in environment variables (priority 1) or encrypted database (priority 2)
- Never read from localStorage on the server
- Content Security Policy headers on all routes
- Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) in production
- X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN
- No secrets exposed to client bundles

---

## 13. Authentication

Guest-first model (similar to Notion, Vercel, Cursor):
1. Guest mode — full functionality, data in localStorage
2. Login → sync profile to database
3. Cross-device sync via database

Provider: Next-Auth (configured but optional for guest use)

---

## 14. Performance Strategy

- Streaming SSE for all AI responses
- React Suspense boundaries for lazy-loaded routes
- Dynamic imports for heavy components (charts, markdown renderers)
- Zustand selectors for granular re-renders
- Framer Motion with `AnimatePresence` for smooth transitions
- Image optimization via Next.js `<Image>`
- Service worker caching: cache-first for static, network-first for API

---

## 15. Roadmap

- **v2.5.0**: Enterprise SEO, AI discoverability, PWA, production hardening
- **v2.6.0**: Real-time collaborative mock interview sessions
- **v2.7.0**: OAuth sync with Google Drive and Dropbox
- **v2.8.0**: Offline-capable AI via WebGPU in-browser models
- **v3.0.0**: Full SaaS with team workspaces, shared templates, billing

---

## 16. Contribution Guide

1. Fork https://github.com/karthikrshet/Career-Agents
2. Read AGENTS.md for strict registry rules
3. Run `python scripts/validate.py` before changes
4. Run `python scripts/generate-data.py` after changes
5. Never edit generated files directly (career-os.json, README.md, maps)
6. New agents must exist in both agent-registry.json AND divisions.json
7. Agent .md files must be ≥ 300 words with required standard headings
8. PR description must include validation pipeline output

---

# App
